Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe one of your friends who learned something without a teacher

描述一个没老师自学的朋友

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe one of your friends who learned something without a teacher

  • Who he/she is (他/她是谁)
  • What he/she learned (他/她学的是什么)
  • Why he/she learned this (他/她为什么自学这个)
  • And explain whether it would be easier to learn from a teacher (并解释有老师教会不会更轻松)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe one of your friends who learned something without a teacher

I'd like to talk about my university roommate, who taught himself to program without taking a single class. He's a really determined guy, and his story still impresses me. First of all, who he is: he's my roommate from university, and we've shared a dorm since our first year. What he learned was Python, which he picked up entirely on his own. He never attended any programming course or paid for a tutor, he just watched tutorial videos on Bilibili and read the official documentation, practising a little every day. As for why he learned it, he told me he was simply curious. He liked computers and wanted to understand how software works, and he felt the free resources online were good enough, so there was no point spending money on a class. By our second year, he could already write small tools to help our class organise information, which was genuinely useful. Now, would it have been easier with a teacher? Honestly, I think it might have been faster in some ways, since a teacher can point out mistakes and answer questions directly. But my roommate proved that with motivation and good resources, you can go a long way on your own. What I admire most is his patience, because self-learning means solving every problem yourself, and he never gave up. Looking back, he's the reason I believe curiosity is the best teacher.

讲的是大学室友，完全自学编程没上过课。他自学 Python，没报班没请家教，就看 B 站教学视频和官方文档，每天练一点。自学原因是单纯好奇、觉得网上免费资源够用。大二时已经能写小工具帮班级统计信息。有老师教可能更快，但他证明靠动力和好资源自学也能走很远；最佩服他的耐心，自学意味着每个问题都要自己解决，他从不放弃。

Q2Is it necessary to keep learning after graduating from school?

Absolutely, I think it's necessary, and it's becoming more important every year. The main reason is that technology and industries change so quickly that skills learned at school can become outdated within a few years. For example, in my field, programming languages and tools are constantly being updated, so professionals have to keep learning to stay competitive. In that sense, graduation is really just the beginning of lifelong learning.

非常必要，而且越来越重要。技术和行业变化太快，学校学的技能几年内就可能过时；比如编程语言和工具不断更新，从业者必须持续学习才能保持竞争力。毕业只是终身学习的开始。

Q3Should teachers make learning in their classes fun?

I'd say yes, making classes fun is valuable, though it shouldn't be the only goal. When students enjoy a lesson, they pay more attention and remember more, so fun activities can genuinely improve learning. That said, the content still needs to be solid, because entertainment without substance doesn't help anyone in the long run. So I think the ideal is a teacher who makes the material engaging while keeping the learning meaningful.

让课堂有趣很有价值，但不该是唯一目标。学生喜欢一节课就会更专注、记得更牢，有趣的活动确实能提升学习效果；但内容本身要扎实，光有趣没实质长期没用。理想是老师既让内容吸引人又保持学习有意义。

Q4Do you think there are too many subjects for students to learn?

I think it depends on the stage of education. In primary and secondary school, students in my country do study quite a lot of subjects, and some of them feel unnecessary for most people. This can leave students tired and unable to go deep into anything. Having said that, a broad range of subjects helps children discover their interests. So I'd say the number is reasonable in theory, but the pressure around exams makes it feel like too much.

取决于教育阶段。中小学科目确实很多，有些对多数人显得没必要，让学生疲惫、无法深入任何一门；但科目广有助于孩子发现兴趣。理论上数量合理，是考试压力让它显得太多。

Q5Is it better to focus on a few subjects or to learn many subjects?

I think a balance is ideal, though it depends on the person's goals. Focusing on a few subjects allows you to go deep and build real expertise, which matters for a career. On the other hand, learning many subjects broadens your horizons and helps you find what you're good at. For students, I'd say it's wise to explore widely at first, then gradually focus on the areas that interest them most.

平衡最理想，取决于个人目标。专注少数科目能深入、建立真正的专业能力，对职业重要；学很多科目能开阔视野、帮人发现擅长什么。学生最好先广泛探索，再逐渐聚焦最感兴趣的领域。

Q6Do you think enterprises should provide training for their employees?

Definitely, I think companies should invest in training their employees. The main reason is that it benefits both sides: employees gain new skills and feel valued, while the company gets a more capable workforce. In fast-moving industries, training is almost essential, because new technology appears constantly. Of course, it costs money and time, but in the long run, I believe it's a worthwhile investment that reduces staff turnover.

公司应该投资员工培训，对双方都有利：员工获得新技能、感到被重视，公司得到更有能力的团队。在快速变化的行业培训几乎是必需的，因为新技术不断出现。虽然花钱花时间，但长期是值得的投资，还能降低员工流失率。

Q7Do you think it is good for older adults to continue learning?

Yes, I think it's very good for older adults to keep learning. For one thing, learning new things keeps the brain active, which may help delay mental decline. It also gives them a sense of purpose and something meaningful to do after retirement. Many older people in my country take up things like calligraphy, dancing or even using smartphones, and they seem much happier for it. So I'd say learning is beneficial at any age.

老年人持续学习非常好：学新东西让大脑保持活跃，可能延缓认知衰退；退休后也有目标感和有意义的事做。国内很多老人学书法、跳舞甚至用智能手机，看起来更快乐。学习在任何年龄都有益。
